class: An async UI handler that reads or resets shared reactive state AFTER an await (or an early-return path that does not invalidate in-flight requests) lets a late reply overwrite what the user did meanwhile. Unit tests that settle every promise before the next action (flushPromises) can never see it; a real browser or an e2e that acts while the request is in flight sees it intermittently, so it looks like a flaky test.
mechanism: W-068 LegPicker save() awaited the planned-entry POST, then read action/lots and called resetForm(), wiping the next leg's picks; StrategyBuilderPage load() returned for no-draft without bumping its request sequence, so a late outcome reply set 'computed' after every leg was removed.

first_seen.evidence: CI run 38065650427: leg-picker.spec.ts:37 timed out on a disabled pick-strike once, passed on retry (called flaky); after a round-2 wait, CI run 38066421591: leg-picker.spec.ts:40 failed at the second addLeg on mobile x2 and desktop x1 (pick-strike disabled, 14 polls), leg-picker.spec.ts:61 expected data-state no-draft, received computed; Vitest 24/24 green throughout. Independent review (fable) traced both to the await ordering; orchestrator confirmed in the code.

fix: Snapshot every input and reset the form synchronously before the await; build the result from the snapshot; every call path (including early returns) bumps the request sequence. Tests hold the promise open while the user acts. An intermittent e2e failure is treated as a race to explain, never waited around.

detection.note: The held-open-promise Vitest cases in frontend/tests/leg-picker.test.js cover these two handlers only; nothing scans other async handlers for reads after an await.

occurrences.where: W-068 leg picker and Builder page
occurrences.evidence: two CI rounds red on the same race before the independent review
